entries.description: The @color-profile rule defines and names a color profile which can later be used in the color() function to specify a color.
entries.name: @color-profile

entries.description: The @container rule is a conditional group rule whose condition contains a container query, which is a boolean combination of container size queries and/or container style queries. Style declarations within the @container rule are filtered by its condition to only match when the container query is true for their element’s query container.
entries.name: @container

entries.description: The @counter-style rule allows authors to define a custom counter style. The components of a counter style are specified by descriptors in the @counter-style rule. The algorithm is specified implicitly by a combination of the system, symbols, and additive-symbols properties.
entries.name: @counter-style

entries.description: The @font-palette-values rule defines a color palette and associates that color palette with a specific font. This allows a web author to select arbitrary <color>s to use inside a color font rather than being limited to the preexisting palettes inside font files.
entries.name: @font-palette-values

entries.name: @layer

entries.description: The @location rule is an at-rule that associates an author-defined name with a URL pattern. This name can be referenced in @navigation rules and in :link-to() pseudo-classes.
entries.name: @location

entries.description: The @namespace at-rule declares a namespace prefix and associates it with a given namespace name (a string). This namespace prefix can then be used in namespace-qualified names such as the CSS qualified names defined below.
entries.name: @namespace

entries.description: The @navigation rule is a conditional group rule whose condition tests characteristics of the current URL or of the state of navigation between two URLs. These queries are called navigation queries.
entries.name: @navigation

entries.description: Authors can specify various aspects of a page box, such as its dimensions, orientation, and margins, within an @page rule. @page rules are allowed wherever rule-sets are allowed. An @page rule consists of the keyword @page, an optional comma-separated list of page selectors and a block of declarations (said to be in the page context). An @page rule can also contain other at-rules, interleaved between declarations. The current level of this specification only allows margin at-rules inside @page.
entries.name: @page

entries.description: The @position-try rule defines a position option with a given name, specifying one or more sets of positioning properties that can be applied to a box via position-try-fallbacks.
entries.name: @position-try

entries.description: Scoped styles are described in CSS using the @scope block at-rule, which declares a scoping root and optional scoping limits associated with a set of style rules.
entries.name: @scope

entries.description: The @starting-style rule is a grouping rule. The style rules inside it are used to establish styles to transition from, if the previous style change event did not establish a before-change style for the element whose styles are being computed.
entries.name: @starting-style

entries.description: The @supports rule is a conditional group rule whose condition tests whether the user agent supports CSS property:value pairs. Authors can use it to write style sheets that use new features when available but degrade gracefully when those features are not supported. These queries are called CSS feature queries or (colloquially) supports queries.
entries.name: @supports

entries.description: The @supports-condition at-rule is a conditional group rule that allows authors to define and name a supports query for later reuse, creating a named supports condition. This enables complex or frequently-used feature queries to be referenced by name, improving maintainability and readability.
entries.name: @supports-condition
